easy.def: To say something is true.
examples: He claims he saw a fox.
She claimed it was hers.
I claim this seat.

more.def: To say that something is true, often without proof.
examples: He claimed that he saw a fox in the yard.
She claimed the last seat on the bus.
The brothers both claimed the red bike.

easy.def: A sea animal with two shells that opens and closes.
examples: The clam is in the sand.
I found a clam shell.
The clam closed.

more.def: A sea animal with a soft body and two hard shells that hinge together.
examples: The clam buried itself in the sand.
I found a clam shell on the beach.
We had clam soup for dinner.

easy.def: To climb in an awkward way.
examples: The kids clambered up the rocks.
I clambered over the wall.
He clambered onto the roof.

more.def: To climb using your hands and feet, often with difficulty.
examples: Hikers clambered over the boulders to reach the top.
She clambered over the fence.
He clambered up the steep bank.

easy.def: A loud, confused noise.
examples: There was a clamor in the hall.
The clamor was loud.
I heard a clamor outside.

more.def: A loud noise made by many people or things at once.
examples: There was a clamor in the hall when the bell rang.
The clamor of the crowd rose as the team ran out.
We could hear the clamor of the busy market from far away.

easy.def: To shout or ask for something loudly.
examples: The kids clamor for ice cream.
Fans clamored for the singer.
They clamored to get in.

more.def: To demand something loudly, in a group.
examples: The kids clamored for ice cream on the hot day.
Fans clamored for the singer to come back on stage.
The crowd clamored to get tickets for the show.

easy.def: A tool that holds things tight.
examples: I used a clamp.
The clamp holds the wood.
The clamp is metal.

more.def: A tool that holds two things tightly together.
examples: Dad used a clamp to hold the board while he sawed.
The clamp kept the pieces of wood in place.
A metal clamp held the pipe.

easy.def: A big family or group.
examples: The clan lived in the hills.
His clan is large.
The clan gathered.

more.def: A large group of families that share the same name or ancestors.
examples: The clan lived in the hills of Scotland.
His clan gathered for a big feast.
Each clan had its own colors.

easy.def: To hit your hands together.
examples: We clap.
The crowd clapped.
I clap my hands.

more.def: To bring your hands together quickly to make a sound, to show you like something.
examples: The audience clapped after the song.
We clapped along to the music.
She clapped her hands to get our attention.

easy.def: A sudden, loud noise.
examples: I heard a clap of thunder.
The clap was loud.
A clap came from the sky.

more.def: A loud, sharp sound, such as thunder.
examples: A clap of thunder shook the house.
The clap of the book hitting the floor made me jump.
The clap echoed down the hall.

easy.def: A group of students who learn together.
examples: Our class went to the zoo.
My class has twenty kids.
The whole class sang a song.

more.def: A group of students who are taught together.
examples: Our class planted a garden behind the school.
Everyone in the class took turns reading aloud.
The class went on a trip to the science museum.

easy.def: A time when a teacher teaches.
examples: I have art class today.
Math class is after lunch.
Swimming class starts at four.

more.def: A period of time when a teacher teaches a subject.
examples: My favorite class is music, because we play drums.
She takes a dance class on Saturdays.
Math class begins right after lunch.

easy.def: A book or movie that is loved for a long time.
examples: That book is a classic.
The movie is a classic.
The classic story is old.

more.def: Something such as a book or film that is considered excellent and stays popular.
examples: That story is a classic that children have read for years.
We watched a classic movie about a dog.
The classic is still popular today.

easy.def: Well known for being good, and not changing over time.
examples: She wears a classic style.
It is a classic story.
The classic car is old.

more.def: Of high quality, and well liked for a long time.
examples: She wore a classic black dress.
The classic story has been told for centuries.
Dad restored a classic car.

easy.def: Of old and serious music or art.
examples: I like classical music.
We heard classical piano.
Grandpa plays classical records.

more.def: Having to do with a traditional style, especially old music or art of high quality.
examples: We listened to classical music by Mozart and Beethoven.
The orchestra played a classical symphony.
She studies classical dance and has practiced since she was five.

easy.def: A person who is in your class at school.
examples: My classmate sits next to me.
I helped a classmate.
Each classmate got a card.

more.def: A person who is in the same class as you at school.
examples: My classmate shared her crayons with me.
I invited all my classmates to my birthday party.
Each classmate read a page of the book aloud.

easy.def: A room at school where you learn.
examples: I sit in the classroom.
The classroom is big.
The classroom has desks.

more.def: A room in a school where a class is taught.
examples: We sit in a classroom with big windows.
The classroom has twenty desks.
The teacher decorated the classroom.

easy.def: To make a loud, rattling noise.
examples: The pans clattered.
The cart clattered down the road.
Dishes clatter in the sink.

more.def: To make a loud noise like hard things banging together.
examples: The pots clattered to the floor when I dropped the box.
The wagon clattered down the stony road.
Plates clattered in the kitchen as Dad cleaned up.

easy.def: A loud, rattling noise.
examples: I heard a clatter.
The clatter woke the baby.
A clatter came from the kitchen.

more.def: A loud noise made by hard things banging together.
examples: A clatter in the kitchen told us that someone had dropped the pans.
The clatter of hooves came down the road.
We covered our ears at the clatter of the dishes.

easy.def: A sharp, curved nail on an animal's foot.
examples: The cat has claws.
The bird's claw is sharp.
The crab has a big claw.

more.def: A sharp, curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal.
examples: The cat's claws are sharp.
The eagle gripped the branch with its claws.
The crab raised its claw.

easy.def: Soft, sticky earth that can be shaped.
examples: I made a bowl out of clay.
The clay is wet.
We played with clay.

more.def: A soft, sticky kind of earth that hardens when it is baked, used to make pots and bricks.
examples: The potter shaped the clay into a bowl.
Bricks are made from baked clay.
We molded animals out of clay.

easy.def: Not dirty.
examples: My hands are clean.
Put on a clean shirt.
The kitchen is clean.

more.def: Free from dirt, stains or mess.
examples: She put on a clean shirt after the muddy game.
The water in the lake was clean and clear.
Our classroom is clean at the end of every day.

easy.def: To take away dirt.
examples: I clean my room.
We cleaned the table.
Dad cleans the car.

more.def: To remove dirt or mess from something.
examples: We cleaned the beach by picking up all the trash.
Please clean your hands before you eat.
She cleaned the muddy boots with a brush.

easy.def: A person who cleans.
examples: The cleaner washes windows.
A cleaner works at the school.
The cleaner mopped.

more.def: A person whose job is to clean buildings or homes.
examples: The cleaner mopped the floors after school.
A window cleaner stood on a tall ladder.
The cleaners arrive at night.

easy.def: A product used to clean things.
examples: The cleaner smells like lemon.
Use the cleaner on the sink.
Glass cleaner is blue.

more.def: A liquid or powder that you use to clean something.
examples: The cleaner smelled like lemons.
Dad sprayed cleaner on the counter.
The glass cleaner left the window sparkling.

easy.def: Easy to see through.
examples: The water is clear.
A clear glass.
The sky is clear.

more.def: Easy to see through, or with nothing blocking your view.
examples: The water in the pond was so clear that we could see fish.
It was a clear night, so we could see thousands of stars.
She wiped the window until it was clear.

easy.def: Easy to understand.
examples: The rules are clear.
Her words were clear.
Is that clear?

more.def: Easy to understand, hear, or read.
examples: The teacher gave clear directions for the project.
Speak in a clear voice so everyone can hear you.
The sign was clear, so we knew where to turn.

easy.def: Room to pass under or through something.
examples: The truck needs clearance.
There is no clearance under the bridge.
The clearance is ten feet.

more.def: The space that lets something pass through without touching.
examples: The truck needs ten feet of clearance under the bridge.
The sign shows the clearance of the tunnel.
There is little clearance between the car and the wall.

easy.def: In a way that is easy to see or hear.
examples: Speak clearly.
I can see clearly.
The sign is clearly marked.

more.def: In a way that is easy to see, hear or understand.
examples: Please speak clearly so we can hear you.
I could see the stars clearly.
The rules were clearly written on the board.

easy.def: A person who works at a store or office.
examples: The clerk gave me change.
The store clerk smiled.
The clerk bagged the groceries.

more.def: A person who works in a store, office or bank, helping customers or keeping records.
examples: The clerk gave me my change.
The grocery clerk bagged our food.
A clerk at the library stamped my book.

easy.def: Quick to learn and think.
examples: The clever fox got away.
She is a clever girl.
That is a clever idea.

more.def: Smart and quick at solving problems or coming up with ideas.
examples: The clever crow dropped nuts on the road to crack them.
He made a clever trap to catch the runaway ball.
It was clever of you to bring an umbrella.

easy.def: To press a button on a mouse.
examples: Click the button.
I clicked on the picture.
She clicks the mouse.

more.def: To press a mouse button to choose something on a computer.
examples: Click on the picture to see it bigger.
I clicked the link to open the page.
She clicked the mouse to start the game.

easy.def: A short, sharp sound.
examples: I heard a click.
The door shut with a click.
The click of the pen was loud.

more.def: A short, sharp sound like the sound of a light switch.
examples: The lock opened with a sharp click.
I heard the click of a camera.
The click of the lock was quiet.

easy.def: What the weather is like in a place most of the time.
examples: The climate here is hot and dry.
Polar bears live in a cold climate.
The climate by the sea is wet.

more.def: The usual weather a place has over a long period of time.
examples: Penguins live in a very cold climate.
Oranges grow best in a warm, sunny climate.
Scientists study how the Earth's climate is changing.

easy.def: To go up.
examples: Climb the tree.
We climbed the hill.
Monkeys climb.

more.def: To go up something using your hands and feet.
examples: The children climbed the tree.
We climbed to the top of the hill.
Monkeys climb trees to find fruit.

easy.def: To hold on tight.
examples: The baby clings to Mom.
The koala clings to the tree.
He clung to the rope.

more.def: To hold on tightly to something or someone, or to stick closely.
examples: The baby monkey clung to its mother's back.
Wet clothes cling to your skin on a rainy day.
The climber clung to the rock and would not let go.

easy.def: A place where you go to see a doctor.
examples: I went to the clinic.
The clinic is small.
The nurse works at the clinic.

more.def: A small place where people go for medical care.
examples: I got a checkup at the clinic.
The clinic is open on Saturdays.
The nurse at the clinic gave me a sticker.

easy.def: A small thing that holds things together.
examples: I put a clip in my hair.
The paper clip holds the pages.
The clip is metal.

more.def: A small tool that holds things together or in place.
examples: She put a clip in her hair.
A paper clip held the pages together.
He fastened the clip to his belt.

easy.def: To cut with scissors.
examples: I clip the coupon.
He clipped the hedge.
Dad clipped the dog's nails.

more.def: To trim or cut something short with scissors.
examples: I clipped the coupon from the paper.
Dad clipped the hedge.
She clipped the stem of the rose.

easy.def: A short piece of a movie or show.
examples: We watched a clip.
The clip is funny.
The clip was only ten seconds.

more.def: A short part taken from a longer film or show.
examples: We watched a clip from the movie.
The funny clip made us laugh.
The news showed a clip of the storm.

easy.def: A long coat that has no sleeves and hangs from the shoulders.
examples: The knight wore a cloak.
The cloak is long.
She wore a red cloak.

more.def: A long, loose piece of clothing without sleeves that is worn over other clothes.
examples: The knight wore a heavy cloak over his armor.
She wrapped her cloak tight against the wind.
A red cloak hung by the door in the castle.

easy.def: To cover or hide something.
examples: Fog cloaked the hills.
The night cloaked the house.
The mist cloaked the valley.

more.def: To cover or hide something completely, like a thick blanket.
examples: Fog cloaked the hills and the valley.
Darkness cloaked the old house.
A thick mist cloaked the lake in the morning.

easy.def: A machine that shows the time.
examples: The clock says three.
Look at the clock.
The clock ticks.

more.def: A device that shows what time it is.
examples: The clock on the wall says half past nine.
I set the clock for seven.
The clock chimed at noon.

easy.def: To block a pipe so things cannot pass through.
examples: Hair can clog the drain.
The sink is clogged.
Leaves clogged the pipe.

more.def: To block something, such as a pipe or a drain, so that water or air cannot get through.
examples: Leaves clogged the gutter, and the rain ran over the edge.
Too much paper can clog the toilet.
Grease can clog the kitchen drain.

easy.def: A wooden shoe.
examples: She wore a clog.
The clogs are made of wood.
He put on his clogs.

more.def: A shoe with a thick, wooden bottom, or a heavy, thick-soled shoe.
examples: She wore wooden clogs that clacked on the stone path.
In the Netherlands, some people wear clogs made of wood.
He took off his clogs by the door.

easy.def: An exact copy of a living thing.
examples: Scientists made a clone.
A clone is a copy.
The clone looks the same.

more.def: A living thing that is an exact copy of another, made in a lab.
examples: Scientists made a clone of a sheep.
A clone has the same genes as the original.
In the story, a scientist made a clone of himself.

easy.def: To make an exact copy.
examples: Scientists clone sheep.
They cloned a plant.
We cloned the file.

more.def: To make an exact copy of a living thing or of a computer file.
examples: Scientists cloned a sheep in the lab.
A gardener can clone a plant from a cutting.
We cloned the computer file to make a backup.

easy.def: To shut something.
examples: Close the door.
I closed my book.
She closes her eyes.

more.def: To shut something, or to stop being open.
examples: Please close the gate so the dog cannot get out.
The shop closes at six o'clock each evening.
He closed his eyes and made a wish.

easy.def: Near to something.
examples: The park is close.
Stand close to me.
We are close to home.

more.def: Not far away in distance or time.
examples: Our house is close to the school, so we walk there.
Winter is close, and the leaves are almost gone.
Stand close together so everyone fits in the picture.

easy.def: Near or carefully.
examples: Look closely.
We watched closely.
The kids followed closely.

more.def: In a way that is near or very careful.
examples: Look closely at the picture.
The teacher watched the experiment closely.
The ducklings followed their mother closely.

easy.def: A small room for clothes.
examples: Hang your coat in the closet.
The closet is full.
My clothes are in the closet.

more.def: A small room or space where clothes and other things are kept.
examples: The vacuum is kept in the closet.
The cat hid in the closet.
Winter boots are stored in the hall closet.

easy.def: Soft material for making clothes.
examples: The shirt is made of cloth.
I wiped it with a cloth.
The cloth is soft.

more.def: Material that is made by weaving or knitting threads together, or a piece of it.
examples: The dress is made of soft cloth.
I wiped the table with a damp cloth.
She cut the cloth with scissors.

easy.def: Things you wear.
examples: Put on your clothes.
My clothes are wet.
She folded the clothes.

more.def: Things such as shirts, pants and dresses that people wear.
examples: He packed his clothes for the trip.
Put your dirty clothes in the basket.
Winter clothes keep you warm in the snow.

easy.def: Clothes.
examples: We gave away old clothing.
The store sells clothing.
Wear warm clothing.

more.def: Things that people wear on their bodies, such as shirts and pants.
examples: We packed warm clothing for the trip.
The shop sells children's clothing.
She washed all of the dirty clothing.

easy.def: A white or gray shape in the sky.
examples: A cloud is in the sky.
The cloud looks like a rabbit.
Dark clouds mean rain.

more.def: A mass of tiny drops of water floating high in the sky.
examples: Dark clouds rolled in before the storm.
We lay on the grass and watched the clouds drift by.
Rain falls from the clouds.

easy.def: A funny circus performer with a painted face.
examples: The clown made us laugh.
The clown has a big red nose.
A clown juggled at the party.

more.def: A performer who wears a funny costume and makes people laugh.
examples: The clown juggled balls at the circus.
A clown with a red nose gave balloons to the children.
The class laughed at the clown's silly tricks.

easy.def: A group of people who meet for fun.
examples: I joined the art club.
Our club meets on Friday.
Do you like the chess club?

more.def: A group of people who meet to share something they like.
examples: She joined the book club at school.
The hiking club meets every Saturday.
Our club has ten members.

easy.def: A stick for hitting a ball in golf.
examples: Dad swung the club.
He bought a new club.
She hit the ball with a club.

more.def: A long stick with a shaped end used to hit the ball in golf.
examples: He chose a different club for the long shot.
She swung the club and the ball sailed away.
Golf clubs are kept in a bag.

easy.def: A hint that helps you find an answer.
examples: The footprint was a clue.
I found a clue.
This clue helps solve it.

more.def: A fact or object that helps you solve a puzzle or mystery.
examples: The muddy footprints were a clue to who had been in the kitchen.
The word puzzle has a clue for every box.
The detective found a clue in the garden.

easy.def: Not good at moving carefully.
examples: I am clumsy.
The clumsy puppy fell.
A clumsy boy tripped.

more.def: Awkward and likely to bump into or break things.
examples: The clumsy puppy tripped over its paws.
I am clumsy when I carry a lot of plates.
A clumsy mistake spilled the milk.

easy.def: To hold something tightly.
examples: I clutch my teddy bear.
She clutched her bag.
The baby clutched my finger.

more.def: To grab and hold something tightly, often because you are scared or want to keep it safe.
examples: She clutched her backpack as the train rushed by.
The baby clutched my finger with her tiny hand.
He clutched the railing as the boat rocked.

easy.def: A small bag that you hold in your hand.
examples: She carried a small clutch.
The clutch was shiny.
Her clutch had a mirror in it.

more.def: A small purse without a strap that is held in the hand.
examples: She carried a small silver clutch to the party.
The clutch held her phone and a lipstick.
He picked up her clutch from the chair.

easy.def: A group of eggs laid at one time.
examples: A clutch of eggs is in the nest.
The hen laid a clutch.
We found a clutch of eggs.

more.def: A group of eggs that a bird or reptile lays at one time.
examples: A clutch of three blue eggs lay in the nest.
The turtle laid a clutch of eggs in the sand.
The hen sat patiently on her clutch of eggs.
